paper_title: One Tokenizer To Rule Them All Emergent Language Plasticity via   Multilingual Tokenizers
caption: : Effect of vocabulary size.
model_annotation: This line plot illustrates the effect of vocabulary size on model accuracy for two different tokenizers: “universal” and “cluster,” as described in the paper “One Tokenizer To Rule Them All: Emergent Language Plasticity via Multilingual Tokenizers.” The x-axis represents vocabulary size in tokens, labeled as “100k,” “175k,” and “250k,” using a linear scale with no explicit units beyond “k” (thousands). The y-axis measures “Accuracy (%)” on a linear scale ranging from 40.5% to 42.0%, with major tick marks at 0.5% intervals. The “universal” tokenizer, represented by a blue line with star-shaped markers, shows a consistent upward trend: accuracy increases from approximately 40.5% at 100k to 41.2% at 175k, and further to 41.9% at 250k. In contrast, the “cluster” tokenizer, shown with an orange line and circular markers, starts at about 41.7% at 100k, peaks slightly at 41.8% at 175k, then declines to 41.4% at 250k. The legend in the lower-right corner clearly identifies the two tokenizers by their respective colors and marker shapes.
